messages:
lina: opening a short thread to capture an edgecase we hit in the lab: runtime probe advertised `kv-cache:v2` but requests to that runtime failed fast with cache-miss errors. we need a clear disagreement policy between manifest and probe and a safe fallback.

marc: thanks. quick repro summary?

lina: we installed runtime with signed manifest declaring kv-cache:v2. later the runtime probe (signed) reported kv-cache:0 after a pod restart during upgrade. some router instances still routed to cached-optimized variants for ~45s before control-plane trimmed them. result: elevated latency and error budget.

samir: sounds like a timing window / eventual-consistency problem. two things: (1) define precedence and (2) add conservative cool-downs when capability downgrades are observed.

sec-bot: security note: treat signed-manifest as install-time trust root; signed probe provides ephemeral attestation. precedence should be: ATTESTED_PROBE (fresh) > SIGNED_MANIFEST (install) > NONE. but we need to decide what to do when ATTESTED_PROBE goes from true -> false.

ops: practical ops: on downgrade from attested to unattested, immediately stop routing to high-risk variants and mark runtime `degraded:kvcache` with a tag; emit alerts and create a short-lived mitigation ticket so oncall can triage.

lina: propose safe algorithm: on capability downgrade (probe indicates removal): 1) mark capability degraded and emit metric; 2) routing demote: move new inbound traffic to conservative variants immediately; 3) maintain existing in-flight sessions for up to 30s to avoid aborting user requests; 4) after 30s, evict any remaining sessions that require the removed capability.

marc: +1 for in-flight grace. need to be explicit about TTLs: maybe configurable per-capability. for kvcache probably 30s ok; for hw-accel maybe 60s.

samir: also recommend we include a short probation period when probe flips from unattested->attested to protect against flapping: only restore routing privileges after N consecutive successful probes (N=2 by default).

sec-bot: crypto caveat: ensure probe signatures include nonce + timestamp and we verify signature freshness before making routing decisions. if signature verification fails, treat probe as NONE.

ops: implementability: routers will need to subscribe to capability-change events; control-plane must publish capability-state per runtime with labels: capability, attestation_level, last_seen, change_reason. routers react to state changes with demote/promote actions.

lina: logging/metrics: emit `routing.capability.change{capability="kv-cache",from="1",to="0"}` and `routing.capability.degraded_count` with tenant_hmac label. avoid plaintext tenant ids.

marc: good. next steps: I'll add a one-pager with state transitions + TTL table and include this downgrade algorithm. can we ship as part of manifest+probe RFC?

lina: yes please. tagging @sec-bot and @ops for review.

sec-bot: acknowledged. will review signatures + replay protections.

ops: created INF-2100 to track router changes and metric additions.

lina: thanks all. closing thread when RFC patch lands.
